idiom_name: omitted argument / undefined, no-op function for callback slots
implementation_notes: JavaScript does not enforce arity: parameters of a function default to undefined, so a required-but-unused argument can be omitted at the call site or passed explicitly as undefined, and there is no class to write. A callback slot takes a no-op function (() => {}), an object-shaped slot takes {} or a test-local empty object, and null is the alternative absent value when an API distinguishes the two. This is language semantics rather than a local idiom, which is why the pattern costs nothing here. Jest and Vitest produce recording doubles instead (jest.fn(), vi.fn()): they answer every call and record arguments, which makes them spies or stubs - use them when the call matters, and undefined when it does not.
pitfalls: undefined and null are different placeholders (typeof undefined === 'undefined', and null represents the intentional absence of an object value); a callee guarding with !== null or using default parameters treats them differently, so pick the one the API documents.

Default parameters only apply to undefined: passing null for an unused slot defeats the default and hands null to code that expected the default value, which is a classic source of unrelated failures.

jest.fn()/vi.fn() used as a dummy is not inert - it records calls and returns undefined - so the test can pass while the path has actually started calling the collaborator, and the recording is never asserted.
